verified_facts: Joint press release by the Department of the Treasury, the Federal Reserve Board, and the FDIC at 6:15 p.m. ET, Sunday, March 12, 2023 (Fed FEDS Note).

The press release announced additional funding to eligible depository institutions to help assure banks can meet the needs of all (insured and uninsured) depositors (FEDS Note paraphrase of the joint release).

Both the SVB run and the stablecoin depegs were ameliorated when the FDIC, Treasury, and Federal Reserve Board jointly announced that all depositors in SVB would be fully protected (FEDS Note summary).
USDC's price on the secondary market recovered sharply after the backstop announcement on Sunday and fully recovered once Circle began processing redemptions on Monday, March 13 (FEDS Note).
Circle had said liquidity operations will resume as normal when banks open on Monday morning in the United States (Reuters, 11 March, referring to Monday 13 March).

On Wednesday, March 15 Circle announced it had cleared substantially all of the backlog and that since Monday morning Circle had redeemed $3.8 billion in USDC and minted $0.8 billion USDC (FEDS Note citing Circle 15 March update).
Chainalysis: depositors at SVB, Silvergate, and Signature will be able to access their funds (post-weekend write-up).
The $3.3 billion SVB reserve figure remains the disclosed Circle exposure; recovery of that deposit followed the systemic-risk exception, per contemporaneous reporting cited on the FEDS Note.
forbidden_inventions: Exact hourly peg prints on 12-13 March other than FEDS qualitative 'recovered sharply' / 'fully recovered' Monday.
Fake quotes from Yellen or Fed governors not copied from a fetched page.
Claim that Circle raised a numbered external-capital round over that weekend unless sourced.
Transaction hashes.
price_or_peg_path_72h: Positive recovery: FEDS Note states USDC recovered sharply after the 18:15 ET 12 Mar 2023 backstop announcement and fully recovered once Circle processed redemptions on Monday 13 Mar. Sign: positive.
official_status: Systemic-risk exception / joint Treasury-Fed-FDIC announcement at 18:15 ET 12 Mar 2023 that SVB depositors (insured and uninsured) would be protected; Circle liquidity operations described as resuming Monday 13 Mar.

verified_facts: Circle USDC MiCA white paper notified to the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution (ACPR) on May 31st, 2024.
USDC is defined as an e-money token pursuant to Article 3.1(7) of MiCA.
As of the date of the White Paper, USDC does not constitute a 'significant e-money token' as defined by Article 56 of MiCA.
USDC was first issued by Circle LLC in September 2018.
From July 1st, 2024, Circle SAS became a second, or 'dual', issuer of USDC.
USDC issued by Circle SAS are fully fungible with those issued by Circle LLC.
Circle pressroom 1 July 2024: first global stablecoin issuer to achieve compliance with MiCA as stated by Circle.
Circle obtained an Electronic Money Institution (EMI) license from ACPR (agrément en qualité d'établissement de monnaie électronique).
With that license, both USDC and EURC are being issued in the EU in compliance with MiCA obligations for e-money tokens, per Circle's 1 July 2024 pressroom post.
Holders of EMT have the right of redemption against the issuer at any time and at par value (Circle marketing disclaimer on the same page).
